title: Employer engagement and training uptake
detail: Employers, especially smaller ones, are not always closely involved in designing courses or offering placements, so training does not always match what jobs actually need.

title: Careers advice that shows the full picture
detail: Schools and colleges often only cover a narrow set of well-known jobs, so young people miss out on hearing about the wide range of technical and vocational roles on offer.

title: Leadership and management skills
detail: Many people are promoted into managing others because they are good at their trade, not because they have been trained to manage, creating 'accidental managers' across every sector.

title: Digital skills for every sector and level
detail: Employers now expect everyone to handle everyday digital tools confidently, while some sectors also need advanced skills such as data analysis, AI and cyber security.

title: Mechanical and electrical engineering shortages
detail: Shortages of mechanical and electrical engineers, at both degree level and higher technical qualification level, cut across construction, manufacturing and other sectors.

title: Keeping pace with emerging skills
detail: Technology, AI and net zero rules are changing what employers need so quickly that GM plans to keep gathering employer intelligence throughout the plan's three years.

title: Green and net zero skills
detail: Construction, engineering and manufacturing are expected to see the biggest workforce changes from net zero goals, covering retrofit, heat pumps, solar PV and lean manufacturing.

title: Widening who gets in
detail: Employers and colleges want more women in engineering, construction and electrical trades, and better routes in for young people who are NEET or lack GCSEs.
